audio_caption: The clip begins with a male speaker greeting listeners and introducing himself as an engineer at YouTube Gaming. He introduces a teammate, Salah Addin. The second male speaker confirms his name and that he is a product manager on the YouTube Gaming team. He says he is excited to share what they have been working on. The first male speaker tells him to tell about "clips."

The clip begins with a male speaker enthusiastically introducing a past period when they "started getting a lot of requests" from gaming creators and viewers. The requests involved allowing viewers to highlight fun moments on livestreams, which led to the integration of this feature into YouTube. The speaker mentions that YouTube is the home for livestreams and VoDs and that they "can make something really special" for both of these types of video. The speaker excitedly announces the launch of clips, a feature to "share part of a video with their own attribution". A second male speaker responds with interest, stating that it "sounds great", while asking for more detail.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker explaining the use of links to share videos, and how it is possible to set the start time in the shared URL. He transitions to introducing clips, which, according to him, allows a specific section of a video or live stream, between five and sixty seconds, to be shared via a unique URL, which will loop the selected segment on the original video's watch page. The speaker sounds enthusiastic while describing the usefulness of the feature, after which a second male speaker expresses his interest to see it in action, requesting a demo. The clip then ends with a short, whimsical musical tune.

The audio begins with a friendly confirmation, followed by one person, likely a male, explaining how to clip a video. His tone is instructional as he says to "click on the clip button right here," advising the listener on selecting a section, scanning "up to 60 seconds," and adding a title. The audio concludes with the speaker typing, presumably the title.

The audio begins with someone speaking, explaining a process related to a "share click button." They describe how to obtain and use a URL for sharing on social media or copying directly. The speaker then indicates they will demonstrate how "clip viewing" functions. Following this explanation, there is a brief musical interlude.

The clip starts with a male speaker describing features of a clip viewing interface, mentioning the clip title, creation ownership, and "two pointers inside the video that loop endlessly between them." He notes that "that just looped," and concludes by describing how the clip view page works.

The clip begins with a male speaker explaining how to exit the clip viewing experience, mentioning options like tapping the X button, the watchful video button, or clicking elsewhere, including scanning on the player itself. He then tries it out by tapping the X button, noting that the video is now playing where it was before. Next, he transitions to describing how to use clips on a live stream. Finally, music plays.

The audio clip begins with a single speaker, a male, describing a live stream of Valkyrie discussing her background and how she started streaming. The speaker expresses enthusiasm, calling it a "really awesome moment". This transitions to a description of hitting the clip button and editing a segment about Valkyrie's story. The speaker then mentions sharing the clip, possibly on social media, and shows what it looks like during playback. Finally, the male speaker transitions again, summarizing that they have shown demos of how to make a clip.

The clip begins with one male speaker explaining how to find clips that have been made. He details that there is a "Clips" tab to click.  He further notes, in a conversational tone, that there's a "three-dot menu" to manage clips, including sharing via URL and deleting if desired. The speaker notes that the clip can be watched again if desired. The speaker concludes by saying "that's the clips tab".

The audio clip features two male speakers discussing how to use clips in video content. One speaker provides a summary, describing that viewers can take a short portion of your videos, add a title, and share it. He outlines where clips can and cannot be used based on factors such as kids' content, live streams, and premieres. The second speaker agrees, adding that clips playback on top of the video, maintaining monetization settings, and allowing one-tap access to the full video. The first speaker agrees again, predicting that livestreaming creators will like the feature, and asking when clips will become available. The second speaker replies that they will test it with a small group of gaming creators, then release it on future creator insider videos, and invites the audience to provide feedback on the new feature.

The clip begins with a single male speaker encouraging viewers to try and share their thoughts on clips. A second male speaker then says "First news of 2020". He continues with the phrase "Hello insiders news time", then talks about a "page on mobile". He explains he has earbuds because he started with them in.

The clip starts with someone talking about users and videos, but they are interrupted mid-sentence by a swear word.  A male speaker then speculates about what the person might be discussing. Another "shit" is heard, followed by a gagging sound. Someone requests to "hold on" twice.

The clip starts with a male speaker stating "you gotta cut a bunch of this shit out." Another male speaker laughs and says "so we'll start the interview now over." More laughter follows. One male speaker says "Roger" with another male speaker saying "Your signals coming in 5 by 5." Next, a male speaker says "All right, here we go." Another male speaker replies "5 by 5 baby." After this, a different male speaker responds, "5 by 5, I don't know what that means, but good, let's do it." Another male speaker says "It means crystal clear."

The speaker, presumably male, guesses "Ireland", then says "don't make no sense", and excitedly announces, "It's Friday", followed by a short, bouncy musical interlude.
